title: Counting Bushels Across a Member's Storage Position
content:
Licensed space is finite, so bushels held under Grain Storage and Conditioning Agreements are counted across the member's whole storage position rather than agreement by agreement. This desk note states how the ceilings, the reserved space and the free bushels are read.

## The rule

Each agreement carries its own ceiling, and programmes that reserve space carry a capacity share as well. Bushels taken in under an agreement never pass that agreement's ceiling. Where a programme reserves a capacity share the member may hold that share even when the house is full, while bushels above the share are taken only as ordinary space allows.

Bushels free to move are what is on hand less what is pledged against a warehouse receipt or committed onto a marketing contract, and a load-out is worked only against free bushels, so a member holding a receipt has to cancel or reduce it before those bushels can leave.

Where a deposit would pass the agreement's ceiling the elevator takes what fits, opens a second agreement of the same programme for the balance, and tells the member both numbers rather than quietly rolling the overage into the first.

## The two quantities the desk reads

**Bushels free to move** are read on the agreement as it stands on the day the handling is worked: what is on hand, less what is pledged.

**Bushels deposited in the crop year** are the sum of the bushels taken into store on the member's deposits across every agreement they hold, over the current crop year, which runs from 1 September through 31 August.

## Condition table

| What the deposit would do | What the elevator does |
| --- | --- |
| stay within the agreement's ceiling | the load is taken in under that agreement |
| pass the agreement's ceiling | what fits is taken in, a second agreement of the same programme is opened for the balance, and both numbers are given to the member |

| What stands against the bushels on hand | What is free to move |
| --- | --- |
| nothing pledged and nothing committed | all of what is on hand |
| bushels pledged against a warehouse receipt | what is on hand less those bushels |
| bushels committed onto a marketing contract | what is on hand less those bushels |

## Worked illustration, on hypothetical figures

A member holds 190000 bushels on hand under a Commercial Warehouse Receipt Storage whose ceiling is 400000 bushels, of which 45000 stand pledged against an outstanding receipt. What is on hand is comfortably inside the ceiling; what is free to move is 145000 bushels, and an order is worked against that figure rather than against the 190000.

On a Conditioned Reserve Storage Agreement, whose capacity share is 25000 bushels, a member holding 18000 bushels holds them inside space the house keeps for them even when the house is otherwise full; bushels above 25000 are taken only as ordinary space allows.
